mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business confidence decline.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) signals a weakening demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to decline.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% within a month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as it indicates robust economic activity.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a tight labor market with strong job growth, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment are expected to rise.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% within a month signals a strengthening demand in the housing market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as it indicates increased consumer confidence and economic activity.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2%, it signals inflationary pressure with tight monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as real returns are eroded and borrowing costs rise.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month and FEDFUNDS > 2%
regime_hint: inflationary pressure with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in real GDP (GDPC1) signals a strengthening economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to grow.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of instances despite the positive signal.
